Subject: Follow-up: Redwood eval plan & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we can get a short eval running on Redwood: 

Recap (from discovery)
- Primary use case: automated loan decision support (document summarization + policy mapping)
- Volume: ~1k requests/day, peak concurrency ~20
- Latency target: P95 < 300ms for prompt-only flows, batch workflows ok for some report jobs
- Data constraints: PII redaction required, VPC-only deployment preferred for production

Proposed short eval (goal: measure quality + cost for model variants)
1) Redwood-hosted eval run using your anonymized sample set (10k examples) — we can do a small pilot with 1k first.
2) Models we recommend for the pilot: 1) Llama-2-13B (q4_0) — baseline; 2) Flan-T5-XL — instruction-following for structure; 3) Redmond-7B-quant (our verified low-cost candidate) — cost-first comparison.
3) Metrics: accuracy against labeled policy tags, exact-match on required outputs, and human-eval pass rate on a 100-sample holdout. We'll also track latency/cost per 1k tokens.

What we need from you to start
- A 1k-sample anonymized CSV with columns: id, prompt, expected_label, category, source_doc (optional). See attached prompt set template.
- Confirm preferred region (us-east-1) and whether you want the run in Redwood-hosted or dedicated sandbox.
- A 30–45 minute kickoff with Dev (our SE) to wire the dataset and scoring.

Next steps
- If you can share the sample by EOD Monday (4/19) we can run the first pass and share results by 4/23.
- I'll loop in Dev for the technical setup once you confirm.

Attachments: corebank-promptset-v1.csv (template), redwood-eval-setup.md (runbook)

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the details and happy to run the kickoff Monday. For transparency I'm putting the minimal tech checklist and scoring criteria we'll use so you have it ahead of the call: 

Tech checklist (what I'll ask for on the call)
- Shared S3 bucket (or secure upload) with the CSV (corebank-promptset-v1.csv). If you'd prefer direct transfer, we can provide a presigned URL that uploads to a dedicated sandbox bucket.
- Sample size: please include a 100-row holdout with expected_label populated for human-eval spot checks.
- Schema: id, prompt, expected_label, multi_label (optional, CSV quoted list), category, source_doc (optional), notes.
- If any examples contain PII, mark a flag column pii_flag and we'll route through the VPC-only runner.

Evaluation harness & scoring
- Automated metrics: accuracy (label match), macro F1, micro F1 for multi-label, token-length normalized latency, and cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Human eval: 100-sample randomized blind pass/fail on correctness of policy mapping (binary). We'll provide a rubric: correct mapping, partially-correct, incorrect.
- Regression detection: we'll compute regression deltas vs baseline model (Llama-2-13B) and raise alerts for >5% absolute drop in human-eval pass rate or >10% drop in F1.

Recommended model runs (we'll schedule these in the pilot)
- Llama-2-13B (q4_0) — baseline
- Flan-T5-XL (fp16) — instruction-tuned baseline for structure-heavy outputs
- Redwood-7B-quant (q4_0) — cost-first candidate
- Optional: one larger model (Redwood-33B or similar) if you want an upper-bound quality run (note: will increase cost and latency).

Quantization/profile notes
- For throughput/latency comparisons we'll run q4_0 profiles for 7B/13B and fp16 for the Flan model. If you want additional quant profiles (q8_0), we can add but will increase runtime matrix.

Deliverables and timeline
- Pilot pass (1k samples): automated metrics + 100-sample human eval report within 48 hours of data + access to the Redwood eval dashboard link.
- Follow-up: model-specific recommendations and suggested production config (batching, KV cache hints, latency SLOs).

Links
- Eval runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bEvalRunbook
- Benchmark page (Llama-2 baseline): https://bench.redwood.ai/llama-2-13b

I'll be on the Mon 4/19 09:30 PT call — joining details: zoom.us/j/123456789 (I'll post calendar invite shortly).

Cheers,
Dev Patel
